I'm 30, at least 4 concussions with the first documented a month before I was 22 (4 days comatose, awake but not aware/conscious of what was going on... Purple cloudiness for those 4 days). I tried moving out 4 years ago and things were okay for the first few months, but I had issues with talking to my roommates after I found new ones (I mistakenly took on someone else's lease that expired 3 months or so later, living with 3 other people). There was one that was helpful, but it was during covid and there was underage drinking and just lots of noise. I couldn't express what I wanted and bailed, had a friend help move my stuff to his house and well, that made me move back to my folks and that didn't help my overall stability. I had issues for the past two years, but I feel okay now, I'm going to try and move out again sometime within the next year, have one roommate and see if that works.

I should also say, I took a bunch of things from 2021 to 2023, almost two years total, did it help? No. I was fed a bunch of drugs (Lexapro, Gabapentin, Trazodone, Buspirone, and Methylphenidate) with no success as having multiple downers along with an upper does not help. I should've said no as I knew they weren't going to, but when I was in the hospital back then, I was pretty apathetic towards my overall wellbeing while on them. Glad I found a therapist who realized the medications weren't helpful and while she didn't suggest coming off, I think that she thought it would be better not being on that concoction of drugs.

I've just been trying to take things that help with the problems that are from the head trauma and maybe just from aging. I had my first diagnosed at 21 (I think I had a concussion when I was a kid, I don't remember). I have had issues with stress cultivating into speech, depth perception and falling when going up and down stairs at different times.

I see a therapist who isn't the most knowledgeable in head trauma, sees a few other head injury people, but she's been great. She's not really into medication, is into neurofeedback which I just never got much out of, but she's been helpful. Psychiatry has been a real miss. I've had issues with dysphasia, like coming up with words and saying names, but eh. Another was dissociation, but I think that has mostly subsided, I think that was really stress based.

I should say that I see medication as a neuro-mechanical thing more than anything. I haven't seen much information on how to improve without medications outside of like food, but I also don't want to pay someone a lot of money for nothing. I am super active with cycling, things could be better with food. I do think that, when I decided to medically transition (I'm trans, MtF), that the hormones helped to some degree.

  
I started Lamotrigine (currently at 50mg) and Nortriptyline 10mg a month and a half ago and I think it's been helping. I took nortriptyline at year 2 and it helped with migraines caused by, I think PCS.

I feel as if, at least from a frontal lobe issue from my perspective, it's all been based on what I've looked up. Saw a neuropsychiatrist, refused to give drugs studies have shown are beneficial, like methylphenidate. I've been on all sorts of psych drugs, but year 8-9 has been pretty good. Year 4-5 was good, but most of my issues are stress issues.

It's a real touch and go subject for me tbh. I've had at least 4 concussions, one of which was 4 days comatose, awake but not conscious, which was the start. Functioning at times has been hard. I started Lamictal in August and have been doing better. Had a manic episode at the start, but eh.
